characterization_methods.key_findings: Polycrystalline Fe-Al alloys showed a coarse grain structure with grain sizes of the order of 1 mm; as-cast alloys contained no second phases.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Specimens etched by an alcoholic 10% nitric acid solution
characterization_methods.purpose: Metallographic inspection to reveal grain boundaries and precipitates
Studying fracture surfaces and qualitative precipitate analysis
characterization_methods.technique: scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis

characterization_methods.key_findings: Alloy compositions were usually determined by ICP; for the nominal 10 at.% Al alloy the real Al and C contents are reported as not determined (n.d.).

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Binary Fe-Al alloys prepared by vacuum induction melting in Al2O3 crucibles using Fe with 99.99% purity (purified by zone melting to minimise impurity content) and Al with 99.999% purity.
Solidified in Cu moulds to obtain rods usually with 18 mm diameter.
Material used in the as-cast condition without any subsequent heat treatment (baseline state for the polycrystalline Fe-Al alloys).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Yield stress determined as 0.2% proof stress in compression with total straining of at least 5%; tensile specimens cylindrical, turned according to DIN 50125.
measurement_conditions.strain_rate: compression: 10^-4 s^-1 and 10^-2 s^-1; tension: 10^-4 s^-1

structures.overall_structure: Polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al alloy with a coarse grain structure (grain sizes of the order of 1 mm); as-cast alloys contained no second phases.

unmapped_findings: Nominal composition of this sample is 10 at.% Al (polycrystalline row of Table 1); the real Al content (at.% and wt.-%) and the C content are reported as not determined (n.d.).

For the polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al alloys (family including this 10 at.% Al composition), the yield stress increases linearly with Al content up to 18 at.% at room temperature at both compression rates, with an increase of 21 MPa per unit % Al at 10^-2 s^-1 and 23 MPa per unit % Al at 10^-4 s^-1 (Fig. 3).

The solid-solution hardening coefficient for polycrystalline alloys with Al contents 0-18 at.% is about 2.2 GPa (Figs 3 and 5), and is not sensitive to deformation rate (Fig. 3) or temperature (Fig. 5); this is attributed to solid-solution hardening described by Suzuki's theory.

For the polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al alloys the tensile yield stress equals the compressive yield stress at the same rate and temperature, and the ultimate tensile strength parallels the yield stress; at -100 °C the yield stress and ultimate tensile strength are higher than at room temperature by about 80 MPa.

Ductility (elongation before necking and fracture strain) of the polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al alloys decreases with increasing Al content; a transition from ductile fracture with necking to brittle fracture without necking occurs at 15-18 at.% Al at room temperature and 12-14 at.% Al at -100 °C.

Short-range ordering, controlled by heat treatments below 600 °C, has no major impact on the deformation behaviour of the Fe-Al alloys; only heat treatments above 600 °C affect the mechanical behaviour significantly. Quenching from high temperature produces excess vacancies that contribute to hardening and heal out only slowly.
Deformation twinning at low temperatures occurs the more readily the lower the temperature and the higher the Al content; at -100 °C it occurred for Al contents in the range 11-18 at.%.
